The search endpoint returned no results, so I’m checking Wikipedia directly for the Moon’s minimum perigee value and Kipchoge’s record time before recalculating.
I’ll query Wikipedia’s search tool directly, then use the returned values in the calculation.
```python
wikipedia_data = await wikipedia_search("Moon Eliud Kipchoge", max_results=5)
print(wikipedia_data)
```
Wikipedia search returned no usable result through the prior endpoint, so I’m fetching the two known Wikipedia pages directly.
```python
moon_page = await web_fetch("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon", max_chars=12000)
print(moon_page)
```
The direct page lookup is the next source check; I’ll inspect the Moon page for the minimum perigee entry.
```python
moon_page = await web_fetch("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon", max_chars=12000)
print(moon_page)
```
356400 km perigee / (42.195 km ÷ 2.011 hours) = 16992 hours, which rounds to 17000 hours.
